sol.section: §10 TDL-7 and TDL-10; §18.2; Appendix A A11
sol.problem: The BD3-2 replacement makes loop flags and per-iteration conditions "declared control outputs with TDL-8 lifetime: leak-exempt, unmeasured until program end". This drops the previously correct obligation to clean control workspace before action return. Consider a successful, sufficiently budgeted action B: for (i=0; i<n; ++i) X(z), with n supported only on 0 and 2 and z initially 0. Its net source action is identity on this domain. The two nontrivial continuation flags are 00 on n=0 and 11 on n=2. Retention produces (|n=0,z=0,00>+|n=2,z=0,11>)/sqrt(2), rather than (|0,0>+|2,0>)/sqrt(2) tensor clean workspace. This is observable without direct access to arena wires: prepare arena n=2 under a |+> source control c, run B under a separate basis-one control, undo the preparation of n, then H(c) and measure c. Retained flags give P(c=1)=1/2; the promised unitary gives 0. There is no fault or source measurement in B. An independent checked ISA-0.8 run-action probe of the reduced sequence H(n[1]); CX(n[1],c0); CX(n[1],c1); CX(c0,z); CX(c1,z); H(n[1]) returns four amplitudes of magnitude 1/2, hence P(n[1]=1)=1/2. Uncomputing c1,c0 before the final H returns only basis tuple 00000 with amplitude 1. The new compute witness does clean its flags, but does not test successful forward return. NS §4.2 and ISA §§5.3/6.2 require control workspace restored; an implicit program-end measurement channel narrows that contract.
sol.fix: In TDL-7/10 and §18.2 state: "Conditions, continuation flags and preserved trajectory records of a successful Co loop are control workspace. They MUST be uncomputed within their dependency-validity windows and before the enclosing successful action returns; declaring them compiler outputs does not exempt them. For conditions reconstructed from preserved inputs, compute bounded conditions/flags out of place, apply the controlled bodies, then reverse their exact computing sequences after the last dependent use. For overwritten trajectory inputs, retain/reconstruct the required bounded versions and clean the control computation while those versions are available, restoring the trajectory workspace as well. The same obligation applies to standalone adj and compute. Genuine measurement records and actual fault outputs keep their existing separate lifetimes." Keep the structured inverse rule, but remove the blanket program-end control-output exemption. Operations that are not bijective on their declared interface use the existing out-of-place/compute distinction, not a hidden measurement channel; do not reject Co loops as a class. Add the witness above: all codes 0, z=0, P(c=1)=0, and all loop flags/trajectory workspace clean at return.

sol.section: §17.1 live allocations; §17.3 shadow stack; §16.4 memory rows; §8.5 replay
sol.problem: §17.1 says a shadow-stack frame is a live allocation only "from its push to its pop", with every access wholly in one live allocation. §17.3 obtains one persistent heap backing block with ss_init; push/pop are ordinary runtime operations inside it. §16.4 adds logical validation only for coh addresses; other accesses use ISA boundscheck/load/store, whose allocation table still contains the whole live backing block. A pointer from a popped frame is therefore accepted by the map. At the materialisation boundary use f: p=ss_push(1,1); store i8 7,p; ss_pop(p); return p; caller: p=f(); return load i8,p, with no replacement live frame covering p. The dialect model requires fault 7/payload 0. Updating the stack pointer does not change the ISA allocation table, so the mapped load succeeds with 7. Independently, a checked ISA microprobe allocates a 16-byte backing block, stores 7 in its one-byte first frame, calls a pop lproc restoring the stack pointer to zero, then executes the prescribed boundscheck/load: code=0,payload=7,steps=18 at budget 100,16,128,8. This isolates the absent logical check; it is not claimed to implement the general stack runtime. Reads spanning distinct frames, unused stack capacity, or ranges released by stackrestore have the same issue. The arena fix does not cover this non-coh backing block.
sol.fix: In §17.3/§16.4 state: "Shadow-stack backing storage is physical storage, not a program allocation. Maintain logical frame base, extent and liveness, including dynamic extensions and save/restore state. Before every program access into shadow-stack backing storage, require the entire nonwrapping byte range to be contained in one currently live logical frame/allocation under §17.1; otherwise fault 7 before access or mutation. A live backing-block ISA entry is insufficient. Push registers logical liveness; pop invalidates that frame and every younger frame; restore invalidates released ranges. Runtime bookkeeping accesses use an explicit internal path." Default to an ordinary materialised validation helper, charging its rows in the reference object and providing the same semantics in the native comparison build. Include logical frame metadata in §8.5 entry replay. Add the f/caller witness: payload=0/code=7 after pop; while live, load returns 7/code=0. A second viable design allocates/frees frames as separate ISA allocations, but must revise both builds and replay to keep addresses identical; I would preserve the current stack layout and add logical checks.

sol.problem: The static file identifies a root as (site s, reusable instance index k<N(s)), assigns the root its register tag, and allocation "picks a free instance index". Allocation generations are lost: a saved tag from a freed allocation becomes the tag of a later live allocation in the same slot. This contradicts §6.2 ("a stale copy, a freed register" traps T-DEAD) and §6.3 identity comparison. Concrete witness: entry has nonescaping alloca ptr saved and slot; loop has i=phi [0,entry],[next,first]; h=qalloc(0,1); store h,slot; on i=0, store h,saved; qfree(h); next=i+1; jump loop; on i=1, old=load saved; gate(X,old,0); gate(X,old,0); qfree(h); return. All ROOT(s) memory is in nonescaping allocas, and every path from s to s again or return passes a qfree whose provenance is exactly {s}; §6.5 therefore gives N(s)=1. On iteration two the prescribed static root tag is live again: dispatch accepts old and flips the new register twice, completing cleanly. Reference semantics must trap T-DEAD at the first old-handle gate because old denotes the first, freed allocation. LLVM 18/23 verify this module and the repository recogniser returns accept. This source should remain accepted; its specified runtime error must be preserved.
sol.fix: In §6.1/§6.5 state: "A static register-file slot is storage for successive allocations, not their identity. Each allocation has a generation-specific opaque tag. Reallocating a slot changes its current tag; saved values continue to denote their original generation. Marker dispatch checks current generation and liveness and otherwise traps T-DEAD. Equality compares allocation identity, not slot index. A tag MUST NOT be recycled while an observable stale copy can remain." Default to a CC table of current tags per slot and a fresh-tag allocator; no new quantum ISA operation is required. Recycle tags only once old copies are proven unobservable, never by wrapping onto an observable generation. Add the two-iteration witness: N(s)=1 physical slot remains sufficient, the first stale marker reports code 4/T-DEAD before changing the second register; saved-old versus current-new equality is false if compared before the marker. Alternatively do not reuse a slot while stale aliases can be observed, revising the bound to include retired identities; I would separate generation tags from physical slots to preserve N(s)=1 reuse.

codex.section: Section 10 TDL-7 and TDL-10; section 18.2; Appendix A A11; north star section 4.2
codex.problem: The round-2 fix now says that Co-loop flags and per-iteration conditions are "explicit declared control outputs with TDL-8 lifetime", unmeasured until program end. This solves the local leak problem by changing an ordinary action into an instrument with hidden history. Consider B: for (i=0; i<n; ++i) { X(t); X(t); }, with n a preserved Co byte supported on 0 and 1 and a sufficient budget. B is the identity on all program data and has no user measurement or nonzero fault. Prepare an external c in |+>, prepare arena n=0 and t=0, and coherently XOR c into n. Apply B under a separate control fixed to 1, then coherently XOR c into n again, restoring n=0; finally H(c) and measure c. The retained first condition/flag records n=c, so the prescribed implementation yields P(c=0)=P(c=1)=1/2. With restored control workspace, B is the identity and P(c=0)=1. Measuring the flag only at program end does not restore the lost interference. The supplied ISA interpreter accepted both small circuit probes: retention gave amplitudes +/-1/2 on four states, while cleanup gave the all-zero state with amplitude 1. The new standalone-adjoint rule also does not erase a prior forward invocation's retained flags. This contradicts north star section 4.2, which requires restored control workspace and adjoint=U-dagger, even for this simple loop whose inputs are unchanged.
codex.fix: Replace the ordinary-control-output exception in TDL-7/TDL-10 and A11 with: "Continuation flags, per-iteration conditions and preserved trajectory records are control workspace, not implicit action outputs. A successful standalone action restores them before returning. If conditions depend on preserved inputs, uncompute them with their exact computing slices after the controlled bodies. Otherwise the complete bounded loop must satisfy the action's bounded-inverse and clean-workspace obligation; reconstruct the trajectory using that inverse and erase its records. In compute, the original trajectory may be retained only through use and is cleaned by the matching adjoint(E_f). No trip-count record is measured merely because the program ends." Preserve actual fault outputs and explicitly requested measurement channels. Do not reject a loop just for a Co trip count. Add the stated identity-loop interference witness with P(c=0)=1, no retained control bits and no T-CLEAN/T-LEAK. Keeping history instead would require an explicit north-star amendment and opt-in channel interface; I recommend restoring the existing unitary contract.

codex.section: Sections 7.5(a) and 18.2, standalone adjoint of deferred-measurement records
codex.problem: Section 18.2 says that a standalone adjoint emits a fresh qcopy "before every adjointed event that depends on it", with placement "constrained before their first reversed consumer". It does not fix the record's order relative to other reversed events that mutate the measured source. With defer enabled, take f: m=measure(q); if(m) X(t); H(q), using foreign q and t. Start adj(f) with q=|+>, t=0. The ordinary reversed events are H(q), then CX(record,t). Both A=[qcopy(q,record), H(q), CX(record,t)] and B=[H(q), qcopy(q,record), CX(record,t)] retain the record, preserve the ordinary reversed order and put the copy before every consumer. A gives P(q=1)=P(t=1)=1/2; B gives q=t=record=0 with certainty. Measuring the record at the same permitted boundary does not remove the difference. I hashed and checked both three-wire objects and ran them with the supplied ISA interpreter; these distributions were reproduced. The round-2 unused-measure-only witness does not decide this ordering.
codex.fix: Give section 18.2 a complete deterministic insertion convention. I would state: "Keep non-record events in reverse-list order. Insert each deferred-measurement record immediately before its earliest reversed consumer; if it has no consumer, keep its reversed source position. Source order orders independent records only when they occupy the same insertion gap. Producer dependencies also constrain record placement. Extend local source-wire lifetimes by hoisting required unconditional inverse allocations before their copies and retaining the wires through their last use; record placement is not permission to commute a copy across an arbitrary quantum operation. Optimisations must preserve the resulting complete instrument." For the witness this selects H(q); qcopy(q,record); CX(record,t), with P(q=0,t=0,record=0)=1. An explicitly specified entry-copy convention would instead select the 50/50 instrument for this foreign-wire witness; either is a semantic choice, not a scheduling optimisation. I recommend the latest-before-consumer convention and a checked interleaving witness, while retaining compute's already-created records as currently specified.

codex.section: Sections 8.2, 8.6 and 16.2, oracle shapes with zero payload outputs
codex.problem: Section 8.2 explicitly permits null tgt, void functions and a required non-null four-wire fault register. A shape with no OUT or CONSOLE output is therefore valid and has k=0. Section 8.6 defines only k=1 and k>1 invocations, and W_j exists only for a payload slice. Section 16.2 anticipates the case with "T ... or 1 when the shape has no output", but its delivery rule still terminates with lift.retval p<selected> after computing every projection; no projection exists. For f(){ret void}, the canonical successful wrapper and its charged rows are undefined. For f(){__bennett_nz_fault(4); unreachable}, null tgt and no other outputs must still XOR 4 into fault; emitting no calls because there are no slices loses that outcome. This is a missing supported-case execution rule, not a request for a new descriptor field.
codex.fix: Add a k=0 branch to section 8.6 and its canonical terminal to section 16.2: "A shape with no payload outputs has one synthetic variant W_empty with T=1. It performs the same prologue, region call and unwind check; on success its delivery is p0 = lift.const.i1 0 followed by lift.retval p0. These rows are charged normally. The caller allocates one clean hidden target bit, invokes W_empty once using the caller's fault register, then frees the hidden bit, which remains zero on success and fault. Any invocation control predicates that call; allocation/free are unconditional." Do not reject the valid null-target shape or run the oracle twice, which would erase its fault. Add witnesses: empty void body gives code 0; explicit fault 4 gives code 4; zero step budget gives code 1; in each case the hidden target is clean and there is no payload output.

muse.problem: SS18.2 says a standalone adj computes Co-loop flags 'from preserved trajectory inputs' with 'bounded trace reconstruction for overwritten conditions'. In general no such reconstruction from the adjoint-entry state exists: 'while (@x == 1) { @x ^= 1; @z += 1 }' maps (x,z) = (1,0) and (0,1) both to (0,1) with different trip counts, so the exit state does not determine the trajectory or flags. Basis witness B2 = 'while (@x < 2) { @x += 1; @z += 1 }' with @x,@z Co in basis state (2,2): reading A (flags computed from live-ins at adjoint application: c_1 is (2<2) = false) runs no inverse iteration and leaves (2,2); reading B (reconstruct an assumed forward run, e.g. entry (0,0)) runs two inverse iterations and gives (0,0). Same program, different classical memory. The lifetime is also contradictory: TDL-10 gives conditions/flags TDL-8 retained lifetime, SS18.2 uncomputes the adjoint's flags in reverse.
muse.fix: Replace the Co-loop adjoint paragraph in SS18.2 with: 'In a standalone adj(f), a Co loop's conditions and flags are computed forward from the loop live-in values as they stand when adjoint(E) begins to apply, by forward trajectory simulation on copies of those live-ins. That simulated trajectory is a declared output of the adj invocation with TDL-8 lifetime; conditions and flags are uncomputed against it after the inverse iterations i = N..1. No trajectory of any earlier forward invocation is reconstructed. adj therefore inverts a Co loop on data alone only inside compute (same trajectory and flag wires) or when every condition input is a wire or byte the body does not modify (the ISA SS4.6 form); every other standalone adj has the adjoint-entry flag meaning just defined.' Delete 'bounded trace reconstruction'. Add state=co-loop-adj-overwritten: B2 at (@x,@z) = (2,2) under standalone adj gives (2,2), no trap. Alternative: reject standalone adj of bodies whose Co-loop condition reads body-written bytes (BD-E-COHERENT-LOOP-ADJ); I would take the defined-meaning text above because it keeps the capability and matches 'E generated from the current state, apply adjoint(E)' (TDL-6/SS18.3).

muse.problem: The placement of the fresh deferred-record qcopy in standalone adj is only constrained to be 'before every adjointed event that depends on it' / 'before their first reversed consumer'. Take E = [qcopy a -> w, cx w t, h a]; adjoint(E) applies [h a, cx w t] plus the record. Placement (i) qcopy first copies the adj-entry a (post-h in the forward timeline); placement (ii) qcopy immediately before cx copies a after the adjointed h. I checked by statevector simulation: with adj applied at a = t = |0>, then H(a) and measure(a), placement (i) gives P(0) = 1 and placement (ii) gives P(0) = 1/2. Two conformant plugins produce different Born probabilities.
muse.fix: In SS18.2 state: 'standalone adj(f) emits each deferred-measurement qcopy immediately before (in application order) the first adjointed event that depends on it, i.e. after every adjointed event that precedes that consumer; records first consumed by the same event are copied in their original order in E.' Add state=deferred-channel-adj-place: body = deferred measure of a, branch gate cx w t, h a; invoked by adj with a = t = |0>, then H(a), measure(a) gives P(0) = P(1) = 1/2, no trap. The alternative pin (all record copies at the start of adjoint(E), giving P(0) = 1 above) is also definable; I would take immediately-before because it copies the source at the reversed position closest to the original qcopy and yields the consumer-time wire whenever nothing between qcopy and its consumer in E touches the source.

muse.section: SS10 TDL-2 (coverage), TDL-11 (store after partial observe, observe completion); SS18.2 last-but-one paragraph
muse.problem: TDL-2: 'Coverage is tracked since each byte's last write; writes invalidate coverage.' SS18.2: 'Writes invalidate observation coverage.' TDL-11 observe: 'When every byte of X is covered since its last write ... K(X) = Cl.' But the new TDL-11 store rule says a CC store to covered bytes will 'retain that coverage'. Witness: X a 2-byte Co object; observe(p,1); CC store byte 0 = 9; observe(p+1,1); CC load byte 0. Retain reading: byte 0 stays covered, the second observe completes X, K = Cl, load returns 9. Invalidate reading: the store is a write, byte 0 is uncovered since it, K stays Co, the load traps T-TAINT-HOST code 4. Trap versus value on the same program.
muse.fix: Pin one rule; I would take the retain reading that TDL-11 already promises. Add to TDL-2: 'Writes invalidate coverage, except a CC store permitted by TDL-11 to already-covered bytes: it writes a known classical value to the arena cells and shadow together, so those bytes remain covered, with that store as their covering write.' Change SS18.2 to 'Event-application writes invalidate observation coverage.' and the observe completion clause to 'covered since its last write other than such a CC store'. Add state=co-observe-write-observe for the witness above: after the second observe K = Cl, load of byte 0 returns 9, code 0. (The invalidate-and-reobserve default is equally implementable if the maintainer prefers one uniform coverage bit, but one of the two must be stated.)

muse.section: SS6.5 (reference instance bound, setjmp preamble and rule 2); SS7.5(b)
muse.problem: The new setjmp preamble is function-local ('if F contains a setjmp site'), but re-entry is interprocedural, and E(c) for call sites in rule 2 is never defined (which module/CFG, whether N29 continuation edges count as loop back edges). Witness: P() { r = setjmp(jb); G(r); ... } where G(i) { h = qalloc(0,1); store h into @slot[i]; deep(); } and deep() longjmps to jb on its first call. The site s is in G, which contains no setjmp; on the source call graph of SS4.1 (no longjmp edges) E(s) = 1 x E(callsite in P) = 1, so N(s) = 1. Execution allocates instance 1 into slot[0], longjmps, and allocates instance 2 into slot[1] while instance 1 is live (native check with clang -O2, LLVM 18 and 23: slots = 1,2, max live = 2). The N = 1 plugin must alias the live register or trap where the reference semantics has two clean handles; a second plugin that counts materialised sjlj cycles gets E = infinity and verdict blocked:BD-B-ISA4, so even the module verdict diverges. SS7.5(b) R hoisting inherits the gap.
muse.fix: Replace the SS6.5 preamble with an interprocedural rule and define E(c): 'Before rules 1-2, augment each CFG with an N29 edge from every call in whose closure a longjmp may execute to the continuation of every setjmp site in every function that may be an ancestor of that call in the call graph. E(c) for a call site c is the product of the constant maximum trip counts of the loops of the augmented CFG of c's function that contain c, times the sum of E over the call sites of that function (device entry = 1), and is infinity if any such loop has no constant maximum trip count. The reference default remains conservative: if the continuation of a setjmp site in any may-ancestor A of F (A = F included) can reach s through augmented CFG and call edges, s is not self-disjoint and E(s) = infinity (BLK-1; BLK-4 under SS7.5(b)), with the bounded static-file fallback.' Add example=handle-setjmp-interproc for the witness above with verdict=blocked:BD-B-ISA4 and state {instances: 2, distinct: true, live_after: 0, trap: 0} under the 64-instance fallback.
